observations.reading: First blind reading recovered two records for one request. Delivery progresses Accepted to Received to Acknowledged, with repeated receipt preserving Received. Task begins Open and selects a terminal outcome through Result, Failure, Cancel or observed expiry. Bold states attracted attention first. The shared task trunk read like a decision tree. Selecting between the two Result endpoints required consulting the caption because the exits lacked status labels.
observations.annotation_burden: The large task tree, repeated receipt notes, identity-retention sentence and first-commit sentence competed for attention. The long expired_outcome_unknown identifier dominated its row. Separate panels successfully preserved the delivery/task distinction.
observations.reproduction: Inspected at declared 144.35 by 116.68 mm with 9 pt type. Text appeared legible in the supplied digital render, with abundant vertical space and a visually heavy final identifier. This judgement concerns digital inspection at known dimensions.

observations.reading: Second blind reading recovered five alternative terminal transitions of one Open task. Result: completed selects Completed and Result: unresolved selects Unresolved, each after receipt. Failure also requires receipt, Cancel comes from the requester, and observed expiry selects Expired, outcome unknown. The explicit lower heading and caption establish that the repeated Open labels refer to the same task. The upper delivery path remains separate. Headings and the aligned routes establish a consistent hierarchy.
observations.annotation_burden: Five direct routes replace the common branch and its unlabelled fork. State, event, status and receipt text remain locally readable. Identity retention and first-commit selection move to the caption. Expired, outcome unknown preserves the qualification in ordinary prose. Equal arrow lengths organise the alternatives. The monochrome figure uses position and direct labels for every distinction.
observations.reproduction: Blind render inspected at 144.35 by 79.82 mm and 9 pt. Final revision shortens only the separating rule, giving 139.36 by 79.82 mm with unchanged 9 pt text. Inspected the final greyscale preview, earlier thumbnail and final integrated manuscript page 8. Labels, arrowheads and the repeat-receive loop remain distinct. Figure and caption fit within the manuscript text width and remain visibly separate from the following prose.

initial_reconstruction.claim: The first blind reading identified two normative transition systems for one request: a three-state delivery lifecycle and a separately closed task record. The caption supplied receipt guards, first-committed-terminal-wins and the Result status selection rule. The second blind reading of the aligned candidate recovered both Result selections directly from the edge labels. It also recovered Failure after receipt, requester cancellation and observed expiry with an unknown outcome. Both readings were recorded in messages to the parent and designer before the specification or source was inspected.
quantities: Categorical delivery states Accepted, Received and Acknowledged.
Categorical task states Open, Completed, Unresolved, Failed, Cancelled and Expired, outcome unknown.
Directed incidence represents permitted transitions. Arrow lengths and position supply layout rather than a numerical scale.
There are no numerical quantities, units, samples or statistical denominators. The domain is the delivery and task records associated with one request.
initial_reconstruction.evidence_status: The figure reads as a normative protocol schematic. Its first-stage evidence status was design specification, with empirical performance outside its claim. Source inspection subsequently established that the state relations were derived from implementation behaviour.
initial_reconstruction.scope: The two blind readings concerned one request and its two retained records. First proposed caption: Separate delivery and task records for one request. Arrows show permitted transitions. Receive enables Result and Failure. Acknowledgement releases mailbox capacity. The first committed terminal transition closes the task, with the Result status selecting completed or unresolved. External-effect outcomes require application-level observation. Second proposed caption: Separate delivery and task records for one request. Arrows show permitted transitions. Message identity and history remain after acknowledgement, which releases mailbox capacity. Each lower row shows an alternative transition of the same open task. The first committed terminal transition closes that task. Cancellation and expiry may precede receipt. External-effect outcomes require application-level observation. The final caption appends the manuscript disclosure macro. Its rendered expansion was inspected on manuscript page 8 and leaves the state claims unchanged.
